sources.title: Wasmtime Config API
sources.version_or_commit: docs.rs latest was Wasmtime 49.0.2 at access; release tag commit 3c8a3e79aa3188a1a12b3aebbaa097abccceac92; defaults can vary with Cargo features and target.
sources.locator: Config::consume_fuel, Config::epoch_interruption, wasm_threads/shared_memory and component-model-threading options; Defaults section.
sources.observed_operation: Opened docs.rs Config API and inspected default/method documentation; queried immutable v49.0.2 tag SHA.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fuel is false by default; enabled stores begin with zero fuel. Epoch mode needs a deadline before execution; trap is default, async yield requires async support. Large bulk operations can exceed a slice. Thread compilation and thread spawning are distinct; component async/threading support has incomplete areas.
sources.applicability: Evidence for one runtime option; does not select Wasmtime or make fuel a complete host-side budget.

sources.title: Wasmtime StoreLimitsBuilder API
sources.version_or_commit: Wasmtime 49.0.2 shown by docs.rs at access; release tag commit 3c8a3e79aa3188a1a12b3aebbaa097abccceac92.
sources.locator: memory_size, table_elements, instances, tables, memories and trap_on_grow_failure methods.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the docs.rs method page and inspected documented limits/defaults.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: memory_size is per linear memory and defaults to unlimited; counts and table limits are separate, with some defaults at 10,000. It is not a total process or host-allocation quota.
sources.applicability: Useful for guest caps; supplement with aggregate process and host-call budgets.

sources.title: WIT Worlds

sources.locator: WIT Worlds: component import/export contract and host fulfillment.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the WIT Worlds guide.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Worlds describe the external interface surface, not internal behavior; the only component-to-host interactions are declared imports/exports, and a host must fulfill imports.
sources.applicability: Supports narrow typed extension interfaces; host implementations still validate calls and grant minimal authority.

sources.title: Wasmtime security-vulnerability policy
sources.version_or_commit: Wasmtime main branch, opened as rolling policy at access; no immutable commit captured.
sources.locator: Guest-return validation and denial-of-service sections, lines 191-204 and 250-264.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream policy and inspected host-value and DoS guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Embedders must validate guest values before unsafe host operations; executing guest DoS, uninterruptible loops, panic/abort, and user-controlled memory exhaustion are security issues under Wasmtime policy.
sources.applicability: Supports validation/watchdog recommendations for the Wasm candidate; not a guarantee for other runtimes.

sources.title: Wasmtime CLI 49.0.2 release notes

sources.observed_operation: Opened release notes and compared patch entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 49.0.2 fixed Preview 0 poll fuel circumvention, no-stdio host allocation, fd_readdir padding disclosure, filesystem timestamp panic and async callback stack overflow; 49.0.1 fixed a WASI HTTP outgoing-body memory exhaustion issue.
sources.applicability: Versioned public history; listed issues are condition-specific and do not prove every version/configuration safe.

sources.title: Wasmtime GHSA-j366-h8gg-77pm
sources.version_or_commit: wasmtime-wasi advisory published 2026-10-02; 49.0.0 through <49.0.2 affected, 49.0.2 patched; older branches listed on page.
sources.locator: Impact, affected/patched versions and workaround, lines 129-159.
sources.observed_operation: Opened advisory and inspected exact interface/version conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WASI Preview 0 poll_oneoff did O(n) host work without fuel. CLI was affected because Preview 0 is enabled by default; library embeddings only if Preview 0 linker APIs are explicitly enabled. WASIp1/2/3 are listed unaffected.
sources.applicability: Shows fuel may not account for host interface work; do not generalize beyond this version/API.

sources.title: Wasmtime GHSA-gqmc-89g8-p25r
sources.version_or_commit: wasmtime-wasi advisory published 2026-10-02; patched in 36.0.17, 48.0.4 and 49.0.2.
sources.locator: Impact and absent-stdio SinkOutputStream condition, lines 129-151.
sources.observed_operation: Opened advisory details.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default sink output stream permitted unlimited host allocation when a WasiCtx did not configure stdout/stderr; configured streams had separate limits. The advisory says a prior fix was incomplete for this stream.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit bounded sinks and host allocation limits; current patched versions are not affected.

sources.title: Wasmtime GHSA-c9gc-w9vx-w86p
sources.version_or_commit: wasmtime-wasi-http advisory published 2026-09-24; 49.0.0 affected and 49.0.1 patched.
sources.locator: Impact, check-write allowance and retained outgoing-body resource, lines 129-158.
sources.observed_operation: Opened advisory detail.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applies only when WASI HTTP outgoing bodies are exposed; write accepted a buffer larger than check-write's default 1 MiB or customized allowance, retaining a host allocation for the store lifetime.
sources.applicability: Supports denying network/HTTP by default and enforcing per-host-call byte limits.

sources.title: Wasmtime GHSA-4ch3-9j33-3pmj
sources.version_or_commit: wasmtime-wasi advisory published 2026-06-24; affected branches through 46.0.0, patched versions listed by branch.
sources.locator: Hard-link/rename mechanism, exact two-preopen permission combination and remediation, lines 163-181.
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream advisory and read affected conditions/remediation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Requires mutable directories, a read-only FilePerms::READ preopen, and another higher-permission FilePerms::WRITE preopen; hard-link/rename enabled modification through the read-only capability. The page excludes symlinks as a vector.
sources.applicability: Avoid overlapping read/write preopens; this is version/configuration-specific and patched in named branches.

sources.title: Wasmtime issue 13544: overlapping preopens
sources.version_or_commit: Public Wasmtime issue #13544; issue record is stable, no release tag.
sources.locator: Summary, WASIp1/WASIp2 repros and explicit WASIp3 non-applicability, lines 160-184 and 296-329.
sources.observed_operation: Opened issue and inspected its examples and scope; no runtime reproduction performed here.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Overlapping guest preopen paths can produce different absolute and descriptor-relative lookup under POSIX-like WASIp1/WASIp2 wrappers. The report says raw capability-oriented WASI is not itself a sandbox escape and does not claim the same issue for raw WASIp3.
sources.applicability: Review the entire capability topology; prefer one private job root and no overlapping preopens.

sources.title: WASI filesystem interface
sources.version_or_commit: Immutable WebAssembly/WASI commit 90105ffc2a4eed594909f9df2f473596500b49d2; interface wasi:filesystem/types@0.3.1.
sources.locator: Relative descriptor paths and host-dependent filesystem semantics, lines 263-278.
sources.observed_operation: Resolved main to an immutable commit via GitHub API, opened that permalink and read the filesystem interface.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Paths are relative to directory descriptors; escape traversal/symlinks fail not-permitted. Path case, unlink with open handles, and durability/atomicity under concurrent writers vary by OS/filesystem; the spec recommends a database/key-value store for well-defined portable behavior.
sources.applicability: Capability scope does not make host filesystem semantics identical.

sources.title: WASI testsuite writing-tests guide
sources.version_or_commit: Immutable WebAssembly/wasi-testsuite commit 5ea11d8fe958beb60fb871d6852ae020e45c0433.
sources.locator: Version-specific paths, per-test root preopen and cleanup, lines 197-216.
sources.observed_operation: Resolved repository main commit and opened the exact commit permalink.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tests live under tests/c and tests/rust, including tests/rust/wasm32-wasip1 and tests/rust/wasm32-wasip3. Marked temporary files are removed only inside each test-specific preopened root.
sources.applicability: Useful fixture pattern; cleanup suffixes alone are not safe outside runner-owned roots. No testsuite was run.

sources.title: Electron Process Sandboxing
sources.version_or_commit: Electron rolling latest docs; states renderer sandbox default since Electron 20; no latest release tag on page.
sources.locator: IPC authority, disable conditions and untrusted-content caveats, lines 36-46 and 71-163.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Electron sandbox guide.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Node integration disables sandbox; privileged tasks are delegated by IPC; context isolation is needed to avoid leaking preload APIs. Electron notes untrusted content is a difficult case and vendor upgrades are needed for security updates.
sources.applicability: Shows that sandbox and IPC broker must be reviewed together; no Electron choice implied.

sources.observed_operation: Opened official Deno permissions guide.

sources.title: SQLite Transactions
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official online documentation, no library version pinned.
sources.locator: Transaction semantics, default DEFERRED, single writer, snapshots and SQLITE_BUSY, lines 33-57.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SQLite transaction reference.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple readers may coexist, only one simultaneous writer; default is DEFERRED; write upgrades/commit may return SQLITE_BUSY, and readers retain snapshots until transaction end.
sources.applicability: Possible atomic cache/search publication mechanism with serialized writes; not a storage requirement.

sources.title: Rust std::process::Child
sources.version_or_commit: Standard library kill API stable since Rust 1.0; docs track current stable Rust, exact compiler release not pinned.
sources.locator: Child::kill, wait and try_wait, lines 129-191.
sources.observed_operation: Opened Rust standard-library process API documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: kill forces the direct child to exit and maps to SIGKILL on Unix; wait/try_wait status and reaping are separate operations.
sources.applicability: Possible Rust process host control; does not stop arbitrary descendants or impose permission/resource policies.
